bullets: Two new Game Cards, the Coin Masters (rules 18.aa and 18.ab). There is 1 of each, so the Game Card deck now has 35 cards, and both are in the deck from the first cycle. You keep a Coin Master in your hand as a lasting bonus; it is never played and does not use your one card play per turn.

Coin Master (Selling a Card): while you hold it, every card you sell (other than this one) pays 3 Gold instead of 2. Selling the Coin Master itself pays the normal 2 Gold and ends the bonus. Gold from Resource cards is unchanged.

Coin Master (Unused Actions): while you hold it at the end of your Actions, you get 1 extra Gold if you left any action unused — 3 Gold for taking no actions, 2 Gold for taking one, nothing for taking both.
The Coin Master is shown when you take its extra Gold, then goes back to your hand. You can hold both; each works on its own.

Emperor taxes you! now takes your cards at random: you lose 1 random saved card (2 random cards if you have 5 or more). You can no longer choose, and no card can be protected — Coin Masters, saved Roads and Walls and a Garrison Requirement -1! in play all count. Busy Little Bee! can still pass it on, and the new victim is taxed at random too.

Fixed: an Assassin! strike on natives already worn down in battle now kills troops that are actually there. A Carthage at 5 of 10 natives drops to 3 of 8 (not 5 of 8), and it can only heal back up to 8.
title: Coin Master cards, a random Emperor's tax, and an Assassin fix

bullets: New rule 16.o, Carthage is destroyed for good: once a Senate Decree battle destroys Carthage, Game Rolls 2 and 9 do nothing except show "The Senate is satisfied with Carthage’s destruction! No decrees for now." — no Senate Decree, Rome Roll, tax, Rome Is Displeased card, reward or Game Card. Each player who sent a legion still gains +1 Prestige once, and Carthage still turns neutral with 5 troops. Only Roma's defeat resets this; if Carthage then comes back as a native province, Senate Decrees on 2 and 9 return. A Carthage a player conquers in a normal attack works as before.
title: Carthage is destroyed for good (16.o)

bullets: On desktop, the game-over popup now fills the screen with the winning general's victory image, with the IMPERATOR! title, winner line, final standings and buttons laid over the top of it — the table sits on a dark panel (30% background) so it stays readable while the artwork shows through.
title: Victory image fills the desktop game-over screen

bullets: When a player wins, the game-over popup now shows that general's own victory image above the final standings — the desktop image on desktop, the phone image on mobile.
When a recall ends, a popup on your next turn tells you your general is free to move again, with a button to move him (leaving Roma he may go to any owned province).
Generals sharing a province no longer hide under each other on the map: their tokens fan out, and each one can still be tapped to move.
The survivors popup now says when the defender fled rather than fought.

Test Mode standings now show eliminated players (marked eliminated), name who met the condition, and rank the takeover honestly among the players still in the game. You can also change your General at any time from the Test Setup panel.
When another player's Rome Roll pays you Gold as the holder of Roma, you hear a ding and see "You earned 1 Gold from ... because you control Roma!"
The withheld-cards popup now stays up for a full 10 seconds instead of flashing past at fast speeds.

Cards given through Test Setup now work at once: a test-given Busy Little Bee! will offer its redirect, and test-given cards can be played by hand. Cards given before this fix are repaired the next time you use any tweak.
title: Victory images, recall popup, and Test Mode fixes

bullets: New: Test Mode. From the start screen, tap Test Mode and the AI plays a game by itself until a situation you pick is reached — like "highest score reaches 7 Prestige" — then hands you the seat of your choice (1st, 2nd or 3rd place). The seed is shown, so the same run can be repeated exactly.

The Test Setup panel lets you change the board before you start — or at any time mid-game from the Test Setup button in the top bar: give any province to you, another player, or make it neutral (with troop counts), set anyone's Prestige and Gold, or give yourself any card (if none is left in the deck it is quietly taken from a player holding it). Impossible values are clamped and a province below its minimum is topped up automatically.
Test games are clearly marked with a TEST badge and the seed in the top bar, and their saves are kept separate from your real games.
title: Test Mode: AI sets up a situation, then you take over

bullets: Fixed: on the phone, the card you just drew flashed away before you could read it — the popup's timer was tied to your animation-speed setting, so on the fastest setting it only lasted a fifth of a second. It now stays up until you tap OK, or 16 seconds, just like on desktop — and only then does the follow-up choice (like "Build now or save the card") appear.
title: Drawn cards stay visible on the phone

bullets: Every view toggle now works for every player, on phone and desktop: guests in an online game get the same View menu, and the phone now has the links overlay and the minimum-garrison label too.
The phone Buy screen now asks what you are buying first, then where it goes — just like the desktop version — instead of one long list of every combination.
Tapping a province now offers only the "Attack here from …" option; the long per-origin attack rows are gone (the minimum-garrison detail still shows once you pick where to attack from).
Assassin! no longer appears as an option on provinces — play the card from your hand instead, then pick the target.
Ruled: losing an ally to a rival bribe costs no Prestige, since none was ever gained by adding the ally. The rules now credit the ruling to the right date.
title: Toggles for everyone, a tidier phone Buy & province sheet

bullets: New: when you are attacked, you can now Flee instead of fighting — after seeing the attacker's battle cards. You lose half the troops in the province, and the survivors (and your general, if he is there) pull back to a province of yours next door. The attacker takes the province, keeps their battle cards, and gets the battle-won Game Card.
The Game deck holds back 3 Elephants! and both Sneak Attack from the Sea! cards until it has gone through once — then a popup tells you they have joined the deck and the full deck is in play.
Walls now defend a province from every side — no more picking which neighbour the Wall faces when you build it.
An allied province below its minimum garrison now shows the same red '!' warning as a conquered one.
New toggle 'Show Prov Numbers' next to 'show links': it overlays each province's Game Roll number on the map.
title: Flee from battle, withheld cards & all-sides Walls

bullets: Chat now shows only the last 4 messages, with older ones a scroll away — so the chat input and emoji row stay reachable even on a short or scaled-down screen.
Fixed: the player panel's saved-resources line could overlap the action buttons in 3-player games, even on a very wide monitor. Nothing in the panel overlaps now.

Fixed: when you are attacked, you now always get the "You are attacked!" screen — with the chance to summon your general — even if you hold no Horn of Titus Pullus. The battle-cards screen also has a summon button now.

Fixed: placing survivors after a conquest now shows the true minimum garrison for both provinces everywhere on the screen. Conquering from an allied province used to show a minimum of 1 for it (its real minimum is its native count + 1), and wrongly claimed both provinces were fine when the origin was actually short.
title: Summon when attacked, chat that fits & true survivor minimums

bullets: In online games, you now see a short summary after the AI's turn, just like offline — it closes itself after a few seconds, so it can never hold up the room.
Carthage is now worth 2 Prestige: conquer it and gain 2, lose it (in battle or by revolt) and lose 2.
Neutral Carthage is now labelled "Under Roma's control" on the map and in its province panel.
When Roma falls, a neutral Carthage comes back at 10 troops with its Walls (was 5). If a player holds Carthage when Roma falls, nothing changes.
title: Carthage is worth 2 Prestige & online AI summaries

bullets: New: a chat window where the "Which die?" box was — send messages to the other players, or tap an emoji (⚔️ 😂 🎉 🏛️ 🍇 👑 💀). On your phone it is under Menu → 💬 Chat.
Player panels: the player whose turn it is keeps the white panel, and everyone else's panel is now light grey, so it is obvious at a glance whose turn it is.
Bribe the Ally!: after bribing a rival's allied province, you can now move troops into it from any one of your own provinces — so it does not sit there with just 1 troop. The AI does it too.
Fixed: in online games, a Game Card you earn on another player's turn now draws itself right away instead of waiting behind the Game Roll popup.
title: Player chat, clearer turn panels & Bribe reinforcements

bullets: Assassin! kills on natives are now permanent: natives it kills never come back, and the province stays weakened for good (a lower native count also means a lower garrison minimum, less to borrow and a cheaper Bribe).

The rules book now matches the game on Germanicus (Fight to the Death: +1 to EACH die at 2 troops, at most 1 troop lost per battle round, and dice that never roll below 2) and on Busy Little Bee! (a redirected troop steal waits until the victim's next turn).
title: Assassin kills stay dead & the rules book catches up

bullets: Germanicus's dice can never roll below 2 now: any die showing 1 counts as 2 — in attack and defence, at any army size.
Fight to the Death, last stand: when his force is down to 2 troops, it loses at most 1 troop per battle round, so the last man always survives to fight at +2.
The battle screen lists the die floor up front, marks floored dice in the battle table, and notes when the last stand saves a troop.
title: Germanicus: last stand & steadier dice

bullets: Germanicus is stronger: Fight to the Death now gives +1 to EACH die when he is down to exactly 2 troops (was +1 to just the highest die). At 1 troop it is still +2 to the die roll.

Target-first attacks: click a province and choose "Attack here from ...", then pick one of your provinces that can legally attack it — the battle then plays exactly as if you had attacked from the Actions panel.
No more double popup for a drawn card: when you draw a card you now see it once, not twice.
Busy Little Bee! now waits: played on a "Rome is Displeased" roll, the penalty lands at the start of the targeted player's next turn instead of vanishing because it isn't their turn.
"You are attacked!" now shows the full battle details: who is attacking, which province is under attack, how many troops you have there, where your general is, and the cards played against you.
Mobile startup choices are now popup buttons: the AI skill choice and the General choice open a popup instead of cramped dropdowns.
New: this changelog — a "What's New" view on the startup page with the version history, newest first.
title: Germanicus buff, target-first attacks & more

bullets: Revolt! and a rival's Bribe the Ally! can no longer target a player with only 1 or 2 provinces.
Converting your own allied province with Bribe the Ally! is unchanged, and the Revolt Roll (the dice roll at the start of a turn) is unchanged.
title: Small-empire protection

bullets: The move counter (0/2, 1/2, 2/2) now sits right next to the "4. Actions" header.
Losing an allied province in battle no longer costs you prestige (the attacker still gains 1 for the conquest).
Placing survivors after a conquest is now one popup with a slider between the two provinces, showing each province's minimum garrison; whether the general goes back is a simple checkbox.
When it isn't your turn and you earn a Game Card, it is drawn automatically and shown to you — no Draw click needed.
title: Survivors slider, allied losses & auto-drawn cards

bullets: Online games now connect through Cloudflare relays, so joining from another network is more reliable.
note: Sourced from the v31.21.1 commit message on main, not from MUSE_CHANGES.md (which has no section for this patch version).
title: Online play: more reliable connections

bullets: Joining an online game is simpler: one Join screen covers a first join, joining mid-game, and coming back after dropping out — and the host picks your seat.
Rejoining a saved online game works more smoothly: the host keeps its connection across Resume.

The rules book is now the official rules file, rewritten and clarified — including that rolls of 2 and 9 are never Rome Rolls, and the five-general roster (Caesar, Scipio, Pompey, Germanicus and Augustus).
title: Simpler online joining & the official rules book

bullets: Connection relays for online play were restored, so a guest on another network can reach the host again.
note: Sourced from the v31.20.1 commit message on main, not from MUSE_CHANGES.md (which has no section for this patch version).
title: Online play: guests on another network can connect again

bullets: A Merchant ship must touch one of your own coastal provinces: you can't buy or move a ship on a sea link that doesn't touch your coast.
The rules text now matches how the game already plays, including the five-general roster and generals moving as many times as they want in a turn.
title: Merchant ships must touch your own coast

bullets: The Sneak Attack from the Sea! card now uses its own artwork instead of the generic card back.
Augustus's card and map token, and the merchant ship picture, now use their proper art instead of placeholders.
title: New artwork

bullets: A general leaving Roma can now go straight to any province you control — Roma escorts him, no link needed.
If your general wasn't on the board when he is recalled, he stays off the board instead of appearing in Roma.
The AI can now play Sneak Attack from the Sea! when the odds are good (it never could before).
Buying a ship is now a two-step pick: first your coastal province, then the sea-linked partner.
Rules wording: only a player-controlled Carthage satisfies the Senate on rolls of 2 and 9.
title: Roma escort, Sneak Attack AI & a two-step ship picker

bullets: Game Rolls of 2 and 9 now follow who controls Carthage: only a player currently holding Carthage satisfies the Senate — neutral or unowned Carthage still raises a Senate Decree.
Rolls of 1 and 10 are still Rome Rolls.
title: Game Rolls 2 and 9 follow who controls Carthage

bullets: A recalled general's token goes to Roma, all his perks switch off while he is recalled, and he can't move or join attacks until the recall ends — house arrest in Rome.
Your general can now move as many times as you want in a turn — still free, still not an action.
title: Recalled generals go to Roma & unlimited general moves

bullets: Merchant Bonus now starts at 2 Roads and pays Roads minus 1 (2 Roads = +1 Gold, 3 Roads = +2, and so on, with no cap).
A Merchant ship now costs 5 Gold (was 8).
The Bribe the Ally! text now correctly says converting your own ally gives +1 Prestige (the game already did).
title: Merchant Bonus starts at 2 Roads & cheaper ships

bullets: The AI now only fights on to burn your Elephants and Moral Boosts when it has enough troops elsewhere to afford the losses — with thin reserves it retreats as before.
title: Smarter AI elephant logic

bullets: New purchase: buy 1 Prestige for 20 Gold. Unlike standing Gold Prestige, bought prestige is banked permanently — it can't vanish if the gold is spent or taken.
The AI values allies more: it allies more often and holds on to Bribe the Ally! instead of selling it first.
The AI now sometimes fights on to burn your Elephants and Moral Boosts instead of retreating and handing them back.
The rules book now matches the game on Bribe the Ally! (+1 Prestige for converting your own ally) and the Merchant Bonus (Roads minus 2, no cap).
Fixed: playing Sneak Attack with no actions left could lock the game — the card now stays in your hand.
title: Buy Prestige for Gold & a smarter AI

bullets: Germanicus's perks are now described correctly in the rules (Fight to the Death: +1 to the highest die at 2 troops, +2 at 1).
The battle screen lists Fight to the Death up front, and no longer claims the Wall is ignored when there is no Wall.
Dice that a perk adjusted are now marked with a +N badge in the battle table.
The General button stays visible until End Turn (greyed with the reason when you can't move him).
Your general's token on the map is clickable — tap it to pick where he moves.
title: Germanicus battle display & a clickable general

bullets: New AI difficulty: the current AI is now "Normal", and there's a gentler "Easy" you can pick per AI seat at setup.
Easy AI never plays Revolt! or Assassin! against you in the first 10 rounds, then only half as often — and it attacks your provinces at most once per turn.
title: AI difficulty: Normal & Easy

bullets: New dice button next to the Seed field, and every new game now starts with a fresh random seed.
A played Sneak Attack card now goes to a throwaway pile for good — so it can happen at most twice per game.
Cards added to old saves (like Sneak Attack) now shuffle into the deck instead of landing at the bottom where you'd never draw them.
Revolt! and Bribe the Ally! now name the general when he is the reason a card can't be played.
title: Fresh seeds, a throwaway pile & clearer card messages

bullets: Revolt! now tells you when the general is the reason it can't be played, instead of only citing the troop rule.
Sneak Attack can now target coastal provinces whose natives haven't been rolled yet — their natives are rolled when you pick them.
The desktop Sneak Attack flow now has a "Review attack" button on the troop step, so it no longer dead-ends.
title: Sneak Attack fixes

bullets: Your general now protects the province he stands on: it can't Revolt or be bribed away by a rival (converting your own ally still works).
New Game Card: "Sneak Attack from the Sea!" (×2) — attack any coastal province from one of your coastal provinces with a Road.
title: Your general protects his province & Sneak Attack!
